customManagers.description: Track Node.js version in any mise.toml (web/, studio/, site/) — captures bare semver; the node-version datasource returns bare numeric so no extractVersion needed. studio/mise.toml uses node="lts" which intentionally won't match.
Track pnpm version in any mise.toml — captures bare semver; the npm datasource returns bare numeric
Track NODE_VERSION in netlify.toml — captures bare semver so it stays in sync with mise.toml and engines.node

Track pnpm version in the packageManager field of any package.json — captures bare semver only. Netlify's build-image wrapper (run-build-functions.sh) rejects Corepack's +sha512.HASH suffix; the matching packageRule below disables the default npm-manager update for this depType so this customManager is the sole writer.

Track lychee (the link checker) in any mise.toml (site/) — its GitHub release tags are 'lychee-v<version>', so extractVersion strips the prefix and write-back stays bare numeric. From withotto.app, with the pattern widened from the repo root to any folder

Track the Lighthouse CI version the site-lighthouse workflow installs (pnpm add @lhci/cli@<version>); it is deliberately not in site/package.json. Anchored to the line holding only that argument, so a version mentioned in a comment is never extracted

packageRules.description: Label every Renovate PR for filtering
Tag major updates for triage (no automerge anywhere; default automerge is false)
Group Eleventy core + plugins (all @11ty/* packages release in lockstep)
Group Sanity core, plugins, client, and ecosystem (studio + web)
Group React (react, react-dom, react-is must move together)

Group Vite, Vitest, and Vite plugins (versions are coupled) in web/. Split per workspace for the same reason as the ESLint groups below: site/'s Vitest runs on the Vite that Astro brings, so a bump that needs a newer Vite than Astro allows would hold web/'s half back too
site/ half of the Vite split above: Vitest and its packages. site/ has no direct vite dependency (Astro brings it)

Group ESLint per workspace, NOT across both. web/ only depends on eslint + @eslint/js + globals and tracks ESLint majors immediately, but studio/ pulls @sanity/eslint-config-studio, which drags in eslint-plugin-react and eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y; those three lag a major behind (all still declare eslint ^9 as of ESLint 10). A single group made the two workspaces move in lockstep, so the studio half being unmergeable blocked the web half too. Split so each can land on its own; with strictPeerDependencies the studio PR fails to resolve until its plugins declare support, and starts working by itself once they do.
Studio half of the ESLint split above. @sanity/eslint-config-studio belongs here only; it has no web/ dependant.
Group Prettier and its plugins (plugin versions are tied to Prettier's API)
Group AWS SDK v3 packages (clients + signers must move together)
Group Sentry SDK packages
Group Netlify CLI and integrations
Group Uppy core + plugins (versions move together)
Cross-file: collapse Node bumps from mise.toml customManager and engines.node into one PR; apply 5-day supply-chain floor (manager-specific dep types bypass the matchDepTypes rules below)

Cross-file: collapse pnpm bumps from mise.toml customManager, packageManager field, and engines.pnpm into one PR; apply 5-day supply-chain floor (manager-specific dep types bypass the matchDepTypes rules below)

Disable the default npm manager's update for the packageManager field on pnpm: it would re-pin with Corepack's +sha512.HASH suffix, which Netlify's build-image wrapper rejects. The bare-semver customManager above is the sole writer for this field — it keeps in sync with engines.pnpm and mise.toml in the same grouped PR.

Keep engines fields as ranges, never exact pins. engines declares the supported version range; the exact selectors are packageManager + mise.toml (still pinned by the global rangeStrategy:pin). Without this override, rangeStrategy:pin rewrites engines.pnpm to an exact latest version (e.g. 11.x) that drifts from the actual pinned pnpm 10.x and breaks Renovate's pnpm lockfile update with ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE. 'replace' (unlike 'bump') only rewrites the range when a release falls outside it: pnpm 10.x minor/patch updates leave '>=10 <11' unchanged, and it changes only at a new major (pnpm 11.x) as part of the deliberate major upgrade.
5-day minimum age for production dependencies (supply-chain protection)
2-day minimum age for dev dependencies
Group Astro core + integrations (site/)
Group Tailwind CSS core and plugins (site/)
Group astro-icon and Iconify JSON packages (icon renderer + icon set versions move together)

Group the accessibility check's browser stack (site/): @axe-core/playwright drives Playwright, and its rules come from axe-core, so they move together. An axe rules bump can surface new findings that block until the finding is fixed or baselined; that is intended

ESLint for site/, separate from the web/ and studio/ groups for the same reason they are split. eslint-plugin-astro needs ESLint 10 and typescript-eslint caps TypeScript, so its plugins can lag a major
Hold site/ on TypeScript 6.0.x: @astrojs/check supports ^5 || ^6 and typescript-eslint supports <6.1.0. Raise this when both support a newer TypeScript
Cross-file: lychee from the mise.toml customManager; apply 5-day supply-chain floor
Lighthouse CI from the site-lighthouse workflow's customManager; apply 5-day supply-chain floor. A bump can change scores or pull in transitive versions that trip the workflow's trust-policy check

GitHub Actions stay pinned to a commit SHA (with the tag in a comment) and get the same 5-day supply-chain floor as packages. Actions run in CI with the repo's token, so a compromised tag is as dangerous as a compromised package
